searches.reason: Develop controlled history perturbations—removing recent repeated interactions, older isolated events, or sequence order—to test whether recommendations depend on evidence users consider relevant. Pair rank changes with held-out training-prefix prediction and component ablations to distinguish useful temporal sensitivity from arbitrary instability, without claiming causal identification.

searches.reason: Translate qualitative rejection reasons into evidence-backed probes for unsupported prerequisites, explicit incompatibility, and redundant recommendations. Seek methods using only histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps, with abstention when evidence is insufficient. Validate a small reason taxonomy on the twenty feedback users, keeping observed feedback separate from automated proxy scores and avoiding inferred simulator traits.
searches.query: recommendation explanation evaluation user feedback incompatibility prerequisites redundant purchases evidence grounded diagnostic taxonomy selective prediction abstention 2024 2025 2026

searches.reason: Replace dependence on raw training margins with reproducible ranking diagnostics whose reliability is tested across negative samples, popularity and history-length slices, and controlled model degradations. Investigate uncertainty estimates and agreement between sampled-candidate and full-catalog rankings, while preserving the pinned macro validation HR@10 evaluator and limiting repeated validation-driven probe tuning.
